newsitem.title: USA: Economist disputes Miami, Fla., FY 1996 budget gap.
newsitem.headline: Economist disputes Miami, Fla., FY 1996 budget gap.

text.p: An economist hired by Miami, Fla.'s labor unions said Monday he estimated the city's fiscal year 1996 deficit was only $8.7 million, less than half of the amount projected by the city.
Economist Larry Jessup said the city's revenues exceeded estimates by $6 million while expenses were $3.4 million less than projected for the fiscal year that ended Sept 30, 1996.
Jessup, speaking at a meeting of the Miami oversight board here, said his estimate was based on financial data provided by the city.
Jessup said city officials were "working off the Chicken Little-the-sky-is-falling mindset" in order to squeeze more concessions from union workers.

The city's employee unions have agreed to wage and other concessions that are set to expire at the end of fiscal 1998. But in order to come up with a five-year budget required by a state appointed oversight board, the city must begin wage negotiations now. The city is struggling with fiscal woes and the state is assisting the city in part with the creation of the oversight board.
Jessup agreed to sit down with city manager Ed Marquez and city financial advisers to explain his lower budget gap estimate.
Marquez said, "I hope they are absolutely right and our overall problem may be less."

The city expects the official and final figure for the 1996 deficit when its outside auditor finishes a report by the end of March. The auditor, KPMG Peat Marwick, has said the final decifit number could change from current projections.
